issue.title: Double-archived plan wedges the bob-cli primary plans clone: every pull aborts on 'Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map'
issue.description:
Proposed by epic sase-1vt (Resilient epic launches under concurrent bead-ID minting) during its landing. The epic plan's "Out of scope / observed separately: Plans clone conflict" section said to file this as a follow-up if it recurred. It has recurred.

## What is wrong

The bob-cli project's primary plans clone (`/home/bryan/projects/github/bobs-org/bob-cli/sase/repos/plans`) has not integrated since about 15:08 on 2026-11-27. Every AXE checks run that pulls the workspace SDD clone fails while rebasing local commit `8304b5da` ("Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map"):

```text
Could not apply 8304b5da... Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map; non-bead conflicts remain: 202611/ctrl_jk_section_map.md
```

The commit conflicts with the copy of `202611/ctrl_jk_section_map.md` already published upstream. That makes it a double archive: two writers archived the same approved plan with different bytes. None of the semantic resolvers (bead, artifact-link, plan-header, revision-pin) claim the path, so the rebase aborts on every run and the clone stays wedged.

This is not a bead-ID collision and was not caused by sase-1vt. It happened during the same incident (the `1hg` agent's failed `ctrl_jk_section_map` epic launch on athena).

## Open questions for the worker

- Which actor re-archived the plan in the primary clone after the failed launch? Candidates are the plan-launch archive step, resume, and host-owned pre-terminal archive publication.
- Should a failed launch's "Archive approved plan" commit converge with the upstream copy? Options are reusing the published bytes, a semantic plan-archive resolver, or not committing a second archive at all.
- How should the currently wedged clone be recovered safely?

## Related

- sase-n3 / sase-kb: closed reports of the same plan-file add/add collision class, from the old approval-time dual-writer. Epic sase-s2 removed that dual writer.
- sase-112: plan-header and provenance conflict resolver. That resolver does not claim this conflict.

task_type_fields.impact: The bob-cli primary plans clone cannot integrate. Approved plans, provenance, and links from other writers never reach it, and every AXE checks run logs the failure (14+ times in 3.5h).
task_type_fields.location: bob-cli primary plans clone /home/bryan/projects/github/bobs-org/bob-cli/sase/repos/plans; local commit 8304b5da 'Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map' vs upstream 202611/ctrl_jk_section_map.md
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed from logs only, read-only. The bob-cli primary plans clone has not been touched.

1. `sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' ~/.sase/axe/logs/lumberjack-checks.log | grep -n "non-bead conflicts remain"`
   shows 14 hits on 2026-11-27, starting soon after 15:08, with the latest at 18:32:51. Each hit is:

   ```text
   Failed to pull workspace SDD clone /home/bryan/projects/github/bobs-org/bob-cli/sase/repos/plans: git rebase failed: Rebasing (1/2)
   error: could not apply 8304b5da... Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map
   Could not apply 8304b5da... Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map; non-bead conflicts remain: 202611/ctrl_jk_section_map.md
   ```

2. The epic sase-1vt incident analysis (plan:202611/resilient_epic_launch.md, "Out of scope / observed separately") first saw this at 15:08:46. The primary plans clone holds a local "Archive approved plan ctrl_jk_section_map" commit. That commit conflicts with the upstream copy of the same archived plan. No semantic resolver claims the conflict (not even the plan-header resolver), so every pull aborts the rebase. The actor that re-archived the plan in that clone was not identified.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1vt's plan asked its land agent to file the observed plans-clone double-archive conflict as a follow-up if it recurred. It has recurred on every AXE checks pull since 15:08, so the bob-cli primary plans clone stays wedged.
